reason: The studio's types union and ASSET_CATEGORIES allowlist could not express a 'friction' category, so the surface literally could not see or accept the kind.
The existing coverage tool parses .tsx with ScriptKind.TS, so its AST scan silently misses assertions — a check that runs but is wrong.
The repo-wide sed substitution was an unscoped destructive write over an overloaded token, rewriting files outside the session's edits.
The build command incorrectly adopts and then terminates the launching session's presence declaration, a wrong write by an existing verb.
Spawned builders ended their turn awaiting a notification that never comes, failing to recognise that polling in-turn was the required completion criterion.
The launch command lacked the tsx loader so the platform could not resolve .js specifiers, and the error misattributed the cause to the workspace install.
The proof command exits 0 on 'No projects matched the filters', so a vacuous pass plus per-phase write fences makes the documented flow unbuildable.
A .strict() wire shape behind a deliberately fail-silent writer discards data with no red anywhere — a bad default in the existing tooling.
The brief's negative existence premise was never re-verified against the live store at authoring or hand-off, so a discharged mandate was re-issued.
check:coverage ran and passed N/N by matching a test NAME rather than the contract's clauses, validating against the wrong thing while clauses stood unasserted.
The gate's check:declared is ordered after its most expensive legs, a bad sequencing default that turns a ten-second fix into a full re-run.
check:mirror-conformance registers only one of the mirrored routes, so the check covers part of the surface it exists to fence.
No claim or mutex mechanism exists for the friction queue, so concurrent adjudicators cannot be refused or warned at all.
check:corpus-content's V=0 ceiling is per-repo rather than per-author, so the existing check attributes a sibling's live drift to the running session.
An existing command fails to resolve the house @path convention and performs a wholesale destructive record replacement while reporting success.
The hook's behaviour is decided by whichever branch the host machine checkout happens to sit on, making the machine/platform state the cause.
Node/pnpm resolution walks from the script's own directory, so a scratchpad script cannot resolve workspace packages and the errors name neither cause.
The delivered sheet and its cells carry no record of the code state that produced each render, so the artifact cannot express the variable it must isolate.
renderArcRollup's fixed ordering places the actionable parked section behind the whole increment log, a bad default that truncation silently removes.
The --real build's 16-turn AUTHOR_TEST ceiling exhausted twice on a trivially isolatable unit, a bad budget in an existing command.
The benchmark's stability check ran but tested the wrong predicate (growthNodeCount === 0), admitting visually changing frames as unchanged.
The parked entry's steering comparative was never checked against two artifacts already in the store at authoring time, and nothing prompts a check at consumption.
The arc lifecycle rule reads only the increment log and cannot see chip-carried work, so the record type cannot express outstanding work that was chipped.
The check holds both facts at report time — staleness and the budget violation regeneration would expose — but passes on only the first, sending the reader to a wrong remedy.
No edge, tag, gate rung or curator mechanism exists that can detect a later ADR falsifying an earlier ADR's prescribed build address.
The shell/tool-timeout interaction with a held-open stdout kills the detached run — a platform behaviour, not the repository's code.
The fence ran but asked the wrong question — branch-diff membership rather than the promise itself — so it reds falsely and passes falsely by turns.
No kind-agnostic, field-agnostic text search over the corpus exists, so the absence sweep simply cannot be performed.
The non-vacuity guard runs and passes but measures opaque pixels over already-opaque ground, so it validates against the wrong quantity.
A Linux-CI rmdir race in a temp fixture teardown reds the job, caused by the CI platform's filesystem timing rather than any branch's code.
capture.mjs hardcodes a steady-state 30s goto budget with no override, a bad default that refuses on every fresh worktree's cold transform.
Bun is installed but absent from the shell PATH on the dev box, so the machine's configuration, not the code, turns the gate red.
The uat run path passes the observe runner raw without the memoization adopt already applies, so the existing command re-runs a deterministic suite per leg.
An existing probe observes a retired invariant and issues a misleading refusal whose prescribed fix is forbidden and actively dangerous.
The rerun comparison ran but checked git state as a proxy for 'nothing was fixed', so it confidently certified a real store-side fix as infrastructure noise.
The measurement file was never typechecked before its output was trusted, so a mis-parameterised call ran to completion and published plausible wrong numbers.
The rung's closing message offers only two remedies and withholds the correct third — delete the unobservable branch — steering sessions toward a harmful EQUIVALENT marker.
The published reproduce command was never verified against a fresh checkout, so it names an asset that is not committed and 404s.
The rung fails to take its documented skip branch on a fresh worktree and is absent from CI, so an existing check reds regardless of branch content.
A flag interaction breaks the documented --discharged-by exemption and the refusal prints a remedy that would mint a second increment for landed work.
